findings.where: "Where we're starting" section heading, desktop first screen and phone
findings.fault: The section heading is the biggest thing on the page. On desktop it is about three times the size of the hero's MantaHostels wordmark and fills the bottom of the first screen. On phone it is still larger than the wordmark. When you squint, a label for three small cards wins over the hero's message and its coral action, and the cards under it look small next to their own heading.
findings.who_objects: A first-time backpacker skimming the homepage. Their eye goes to "Where we're starting" before "what is this and what do I do", so the page's order of importance is upside down.

findings.where: Destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The three cards look like they come from a different site. The place names are set in a typewriter-style monospace face and each card has a thick purple outline. Neither belongs to the beachy turquoise, sand and ink brand used everywhere else on the page. After the coral button, the purple outlines are the strongest colour on the page, so the cards stand out as foreign rather than as the page's route to the guides.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brand sheet names Quicksand and Nunito Sans and a turquoise and sand field. A visitor would also object, because a block that looks off-brand reads as broken or unfinished on a site that is asking for their trust.

findings.where: Hero: the eyebrow line and the MantaHostels wordmark used as the headline
findings.fault: The hero's loudest line is just the brand name, which tells the visitor nothing. The only claim, "The better way to find hostels in Indonesia", is a vague small line above it. The concrete part (merit-only ranking, booking direct with the hostel, and that the search is not built yet) sits in the smallest, lightest text in the hero. In the 5-second test a visitor reads "MantaHostels" but can't say why this is better, or that it isn't live yet.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker landing from a search or a shared link. They can't tell at a glance what is different here or whether they can search now. The founder would object too, because their rule is that the loud half must be a claim with plain mechanics under it.

findings.where: Hero: the coral launch-news button and the space around it
findings.fault: Nothing next to the main action says what the visitor is signing up for: how often they'll hear from Manta, that it's only launch news, or that they can opt out. The button's label is mostly an email address, not a promise. The pre-launch status ("Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali") appears only in grey text in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A cautious traveller deciding whether to give their email to an unknown pre-launch site. With no risk-reversal line at the action, they hold back.

findings.where: Desktop: the hero text column against the nav, the section heading and the cards
findings.fault: The hero copy and buttons start on their own left edge, about 230 px further in than the edge shared by the wordmark in the nav, the "Where we're starting" heading and the cards. Down the page the content jumps between two left edges, so the hero doesn't read as part of the same column (continuity).
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning down on desktop. The shifting edge makes the page feel loosely assembled and weakens the hero's link to the destinations it points to.
